analysis:
Examined base_text units of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift (base lines 533-1290) against the complete range map, which shows the only change is the head-side addition at lines 566-569. That addition introduces two stored properties: clusterUpdateDrainID (String?) and clusterUpdateDrainTask (Task<Void, Never>?). Per their comments, they are cluster-member-only state for a supervisor-coordinated pair update drain that owns admission. They are referenced from a new extension, ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain, that is not supplied in this batch.

The declarations alone change no security behavior. They do not touch keys (A-003 keyPair init at base 980), the attestation signer (base 1225-1255), model hashes or advertised sets, or the prefix-cache/SSD paths (T-041).

Integration must examine ProviderLoop+ClusterUpdateDrain and its callers for the following:
(1) Whether the drain ID is authenticated as coming from the member's accepted supervisor/coordinator connection (memberConnectionID, base 695) and is not attacker-chosen by a provider-local process or consumer.
(2) Whether a drain that owns admission can be stranded and hold the provider out of routing indefinitely. Check for a timeout and for clearing on disconnect or memberControlRequiresStop. This is relevant to A-018 availability and to T-053 (stale state surviving a connection change).
(3) Whether the drain interacts correctly with updatePhase, updateSession and deferredDesiredModels (base 549-571), so admission reopens and the update lease is released on abort.
(4) Whether the task is cancelled on shutdown alongside the other tasks.

No regression is identifiable from the supplied evidence. The missing extension source is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
